An Exchange Between Josiah And The "Druggie"

October 25, 1998

From josiah_e@hotmail.com (John English)

I just received your e-mail; I will look at the video tape and see if what you say you said is what comes across on the tape. Taking my son to the football game and will get to it this evening and get back to you Monday.

Originally I quoted the material that I had in writing. Then, when I got the video, I reviewed it, but I don’t remember it well enough to make a statement either way at this point.

Although I do not respect what druggies do, it is not my intention to misquote them. If I cannot verify it, I will check other sources.

Thanks for your contacting us.

Josiah

Dear Josiah:

  1. Remember, the transcript that I sent you is not what I said that I said, but rather what the very prohibitionist National Families In Action said that I said. The key fact is that I have never said that medical marijuana is a "scam." I have repeatedly said that marijuana prohibition is a "scam," "fraud" – etc..
  2. You did not address the four points that I raised pointing out how absurd it would be to attribute such views to me.
  3. You say, "Although I do not respect what druggies do, it is not my intention to misquote them." (Presumably, "druggie" means a user of non-FDA approved drugs.) The gratuitous use of such a derogatory term is worse than pointless. It keeps you from being to understand the views of people you disagree with. I respect people who are honestly concerned about children using "drugs" -- even when I disagree with them about the best way to deal with the problem, but I do not respect the use of libel and misrepresenting the views of the opposition as tools of argument.

I look forward to your posting a corrected version of my comments and an apology to your readers. I hope that you will have the intellectual honesty and moral courage to do that.

At that point, I would be happy to go through your site and point out other errors and the sources for the correct information.

The children of America do need a lot of help, but telling them more lies about marijuana is counterproductive.

Sincerely,

Richard Cowan, "druggie"
